### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eafe6fa8199482582e5966f9a5d1a300a882de9c` — the merge of head `dba2b955eb6954b5e1c6136ff5c23d7253185f93` into base `0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eafe6fa8199482582e5966f9a5d1a300a882de9c && git checkout eafe6fa8199482582e5966f9a5d1a300a882de9c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f dba2b955eb6954b5e1c6136ff5c23d7253185f93 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f && git merge --no-ff dba2b955eb6954b5e1c6136ff5c23d7253185f93

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `dba2b955eb6954b5e1c6136ff5c23d7253185f93`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/30913-scenario-seed-owner-by-person.md, docs/qa/scenarios/README.md, packages/qa/scenarios/README.md, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/prompts.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/units.test.ts + packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts (the `./runner` entry that re-exports `prompts.ts` and `orchestrate.ts`), packages/qa/scenarios/src/schema.ts (`PERSON_USER_FIELD`, `personas[].record`, read), docs/qa/scenarios/service_desk.json and the other eight cards (read, the seed the rule is judged on)

Face: declaration. `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the seven files says the paths decide no face (no clause-② suspect glob, no governed path) and the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides; that line reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset and in the PR body, no `(narrowing)` arm on either, so `reviewFace` answers the declaration face and the tier it maps to is `TIER_DEFAULT`. Whether the `(widening)` arm is the right arm is judged in ② below, since a `(narrowing)` arm would move the face: it is. `@objectstack/scenarios` is published (PR #31221; `package.json` carries no `private`, exports `./runner` → `dist/runner.js`), and `src/runner/index.ts` does `export * from './prompts.js'` and `'./orchestrate.js'`, so `personaHandles`, `personaRecords`, `rowOwner`, `userHandleFields`, `unheldHandles`, `probeValues` and `seedApp` are all published. Read against `origin/main` `0f254f47`, three commits past the branch's base `7c523aa1`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Owner rule (`rowOwner`, prompts.ts) against the ruling (6707625367, Q1 = A′ items 3–5) — right.** A row is owned by a persona's user when it IS that persona's `record` (item 3, first clause), when a declared direct lookup (`expect.lookups`, target = the object of some persona's `record`, `personLookups`) on it holds the record's id (item 3, second clause), or when a declared user-handle field on it holds the persona's handle (item 5, the control cards' route, kept); the first persona in `run.personas` order wins (item 4). An option value, a row-id scope and a lookup to a non-person row return undefined, so the row keeps the inserter. Read over the seed of all nine cards: no seed field holding a persona record id is undeclared in `expect.lookups`, so "declared lookups only" (the #30914 declared-never-inferred rule carried over) loses no owner today; on service_desk the declared person lookups are `agent_group.lead`, `ticket.customer`, `ticket.assignee`, `ticket_comment.author`, and `ticket.group` / `agent.group` target `agent_group`, no persona's record, so they name nobody.
- **Person binding (item 2) — right.** `personaRecords` keys `object/id` → persona, first in order; `seedApp` writes `self.userId` into `body[PERSON_USER_FIELD]` (`'user'`, the constant #31275 landed in schema.ts) on exactly the persona's record row, and only when that persona has an account. No seed row on any of the nine cards carries a `user` field, so the write collides with nothing. The prompt asks the build for "a field named exactly `user` of type `user`" on each person object and to leave it optional, which is item 2's requirement plus the fact that every non-person row of that object carries none.
- **Seed loop (`seedApp`, orchestrate.ts) — right.** The user-handle branch is byte-for-byte the old one minus the dropped `ownerFields` arm: `seed.rewritten` and `seed.handlesAsAdmin` keep their meaning, an unheld handle (`u_tia`) still loads as the admin and leaves `owner_id` on the admin because `rowOwner` returns undefined for it (pinned). `rowOwner` reads the card row, not `body`, so a lookup deferred to the second pass (`later`) still decides the owner at insert. Without accounts (the gallery's screenshot boot) `accountOf` returns undefined for every persona, so no `user` and no record-bound owner is set (pinned); handle fields still rewrite to the admin as on `main`.
- **`personaHandles` split (ruling "Where it lands" item 3, second bullet) — right, and the callers keep their meaning.** It is now the handle map: a direct scope rule on a declared user-handle field. Its two in-package callers, `probeValues` (orchestrate.ts) and `unheldHandles` (prompts.ts), already gate on `userHandleFields` before consulting the map, so their answers are unchanged on all nine cards; `seedApp` consults it only inside the `userFields` branch. The one semantic change is first-wins over last-wins on a handle two personas name, which no card has. No file outside `packages/qa/scenarios` imports `@objectstack/scenarios/runner` (git grep on `main` finds only changeset prose).
- **Build prompt (`rowOwnership`) — right.** The section names the person rows, the `user` field and its type, the person lookups, the order for a row naming two people, the admin default, and the platform-boundary line (no hierarchy resolver on the open-source server, which the ruling's Q2 = C cites from `plugin-sharing`). The old `public` = `portal_customer` line is gone (pinned: no `` `public` `` and no `` `grp_tech` `` in the section). A card with no person bound has no section (pinned on crm with the declaration removed).
- **service_desk pins against the seed (`docs/qa/scenarios/service_desk.json`) — the numbers hold.** 237 `visibility = public` comments, 15 comments with `author = a02`, none with `a04`: so comments go support_agent 15, admin the rest, portal_customer 0. 120 tickets: 15 with `assignee = a02`, 20 with `customer = cus_03`, of which 5 also `assignee = a02` (t009, t033, t057, t081, t105), 10 also `group = grp_tech` with another assignee (t008, t020, …, t116), 5 neither; no ticket has `assignee = a04`. So support_agent 15, portal_customer 15 (10 + 5), team_lead 0 (was 78 through `group`), exactly the tally the test pins. `grp_tech.lead = a04` through the declared `agent_group.lead` gives team_lead the one `agent_group` row the PR's table shows. requisition_to_receipt: `dep_sales` is the dept_manager's through `department.manager = e13`, and among `dep_sales` employees only e02 and e13 are owned (pinned).
- **Docs — right.** `docs/qa/scenarios/README.md` (the `record` paragraph) and `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` (Persona contract) state the rule, the order, the `user` write, the handle/record split and the boundary line, and match the code.
- **Tests and ablations.** 5 new orchestrate cases on the real service_desk and requisition_to_receipt cards through `FakeApp`, 3 new unit cases, one pin moved with the rewritten prompt text; A1 (any direct scope value owns again) reds 4 cases, A2 (the `user` write deleted) reds 1. Each new behaviour has a pin that an ablation reds.

### ② Semver level

`patch` is correct: `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (the card format is QA tooling; no authorable platform key moves) and under ruling A in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` a `none` kind takes `patch` on every introduced entry, whatever the arm. Check Changeset is green on this head.

**`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right spelling, and no `(narrowing)` arm or BREAKING banner is owed.** `yes` because `./runner` gains `personaRecords` and `rowOwner`. The question the report leaves to this review is `personaHandles`: same signature, now a smaller map on six cards. Judged against this repo's own words for the arm, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` DECLARE_BLOCK ("add `(narrowing)` if it narrows a published accept set or public surface", "a BREAKING change") and its GA clause ("a required member on a published interface, an accept-set narrowing, or any compile-breaking change to implementers"), plus AGENTS.md §Post-Task 3 ("`(narrowing)` is BREAKING"): `personaHandles` accepts the same inputs and refuses none of them, nothing on the public surface is removed or renamed, and no caller stops compiling. What shrinks is the answer, and it shrinks to the contract the function declared on `main` — its docstring there reads "A direct (non-path) row-scope rule names the user handle that persona signs in as, e.g. `u_sam`" — so the entries that disappear (`a02`, `grp_tech`, `cus_03`, `public`, `e06`, `dep_sales`, …) were never handles and are the defect this card files. A fix that makes a function answer its own documented contract is the `fix` the changeset says it is, not a narrowing of an accept set or a surface; the record-recognisers' ④ wording for the narrowing face, "make the spec's own refusal real", would in any case describe it, and that face is owed only when the arm is declared. The sibling record (#31275) drew the line the same way: it owed `(narrowing)` for a loader that refuses cards it accepted and a signature that breaks a caller at compile time, neither of which is here. So the declaration face stands at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The changeset still names the change in `personaHandles` and the unchanged answer on the three controls, which is the right disclosure for a `patch` whose exported helper answers differently.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 (reported): ruling item 4's "15 two-persona tickets go to support_agent" versus the PR's 5 + 10.** Faithful, not a departure. Item 4's own words are "When one row matches several persona **records**"; a ticket whose `group` is `grp_tech` matches team_lead's scope rule but no persona record, and item 3 names `group` among the non-person lookups that "no longer set `owner_id`". So item 4 applies to the five tickets that name two persons (`assignee = a02`, `customer = cus_03`), and they go to support_agent as it says; the ten that name team_lead only through `group` name one person and go to portal_customer. The "15" is the card's filing count ("15 seeded tickets name two personas through different scope fields"), carried into the ruling as a prediction that item 3 then falsifies. The dev applied items 3 and 4 as written and pinned both halves (t008 → portal_customer, t009 → support_agent, tallies 15/15/0). The ruling's result for the ten is also the one its Q2 = C intends: the team lead reaches its group's tickets through what the build models, not through `owner_id`. No maintainer round is needed to land; this record reconciles the count in writing, and the maintainer may read it here.
- **Deviation 2 (reported): `Clause-②: yes (widening)` where the claim said `no`.** Answered in ②: `yes (widening)` is the correct declaration for the two added exports, and the claim itself said "the thread reports a yes if its diff adds one".
- **Deviation 3 (reported): PR opened with no labels.** Not a contract matter; Auto Label has since applied `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling`.
- **Deviation 4 (reported) and the drift check: `origin/main` is three commits past base `7c523aa1` (`7fe019f4`, `007fdb1a`, `0f254f47`).** Verified: `git diff --stat 7c523aa1..origin/main -- packages/qa/scenarios docs/qa/scenarios` is empty; GitHub reports `mergeable: true`. The Docs Drift Check comment notes `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` yielded no anchor; both READMEs were read here against the code and match.
- **Parallel card #31121 (gallery refresh, branch `claude/project-thread-3d8sgq` at `de7c89c5`, same base `7c523aa1`).** Overlap on this package: that branch touches `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` (+72 at line 266), `package.json`, `src/export/*`, `src/runner/driver.ts` and `test/export/*`; this PR touches `README.md` at lines 253–268 and nothing else on that list. `git merge-tree` of the two heads reports zero conflict markers, so whichever lands second rebases clean; no source file is shared, so no semantic overlap.
- **Live model run and recorded replay not measured** (maintainer pause; no recording in the container). The seed rule is pinned through `seedApp` over the real cards with the fake app, which is where the rule lives. Accepted as stated.
- **Check-runs on `dba2b955`:** 48 in all, 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure, none still running: Test Core with its 8 shards, Build Core, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint family including `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the one gate the report could not measure locally, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, runs there), Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Docs Links, Flag docs affected, Test UI and Live E2E UI. The skipped runs are the opt-in and UI-matrix legs. The report said the runs were in progress at report time; judged here from the completed set.
- **Should-fix, wording only, no re-review owed:** the `seedApp` docblock sentence "An option value, a row id scope and a lookup to a row no persona is name nobody" has lost a comma ("…a row no persona is, name nobody"); and `src/runner/index.ts` still opens with "Private, like the rest of this package" although the package has been published since #31221 — pre-existing, outside this diff, for the next PR that touches the entry.
- No open questions, no security findings, no out-of-scope findings in the report.

### ④ Design judgment

Carried although the declaration face does not owe it, because two of the judgments above are design judgments.

- **One rule, read in two places.** The seed loop and the build prompt both read `rowOwner`/`personLookups`, so the prompt cannot promise an owner the seed does not set, which is the defect the card's third "Where" line named (`public` = `portal_customer` in the prompt). The rule is keyed on declarations the loader already checks (#31275: `record` names a seed row, `expect.lookups` are declared), so a card cannot reach an owner by an inferred field.
- **The `user` field is a build requirement with a loud failure.** The data API refuses an unknown field on insert ("Unknown field 'x' on object 'y'", objectql `engine-top-level.ts`), so a build that omits the `user` field on a person object has its three person rows refused at seed; `seed.refused` carries the message, and `seedDependence` (#31275) turns the questions that read those rows into not-measured, never a fail of the app's answer. That is the ruling's own shape (item 2 requires the field; Q2 = C leaves grading unchanged) and the prompt states the requirement by exact name and type. Observation, no fix: the gallery boot passes no accounts and so never writes the field.
- **Nothing beyond the ruling.** Global personas carry no `record` on the nine cards and gain nothing; the handle route is unchanged on the controls (pinned "same" in the PR's nine-card table); the boundary line in the prompt says what the ruling's Q2 = C says and cites the same platform fact.

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, 7 files, +291/-56. All files are inside the claim's surface (`packages/qa/scenarios/**`, the two READMEs, one changeset). NOT governed. `main` is 3 commits past the base, and none of them touch `packages/qa/scenarios` or `docs/qa/scenarios`.
